about.text: Roquefort is a sheep-milk blue cheese from southern France. EU law dictates that only those cheeses aged in the natural Combalou caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon may bear the name "Roquefort", as it is a recognised geographical indication and has a protected designation of origin.

how.label: cave-ripen
how.text: Ewe's milk curd seeded with Penicillium roqueforti is drained without pressing and pierced, so the air in the fleurine-ventilated Combalou caves lets the mould vein the open paste. After at least two weeks bare in the caves the cheese is wrapped to slow the mould while it keeps maturing to at least 90 days.
